featured.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
featured.tldr: Rubric rewards for open-ended RL only measure coverage, so models learn to pad; adding a precision term for necessary, factually correct sentences raises win rate over the base model from 10.6% to 68.0%.

featured.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling
featured.tldr: A linear head on a frozen vision-language model's middle layer, trained to prefer a caption over a one-fact edit of it, rivals GPT-4o as a reward model without human labels.

featured.title: Post-Training Frontier Text-to-Image Models by Composing Preference and Rubric Rewards
featured.tldr: Composing a learned human-preference reward with prompt-specific rubric rewards post-trains text-to-image models while resisting reward hacking: FLUX.2-dev gains 69 Elo, and Ideogram 4 tops all open-source models on the Arena leaderboard.

featured.title: Diffusion Reward Models
featured.tldr: Diffusion Reward Models replace the single-number reward head with a small diffusion transformer that samples a distribution of rewards, capturing annotator disagreement and modestly improving downstream RLHF over scalar reward models.
